newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore enjoys nearly full employment in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Singapore enjoys nearly full employment in 1996.

text.p: Wages growth outpaced productivity in Singapore last year, but the country's overall labour shortage eased, the Ministry of Labour said on Monday.
It said in a report that average monthly wages rose 4.3 percent in real terms while productivity rose by 0.7 percent.
"For wage increases to be sustainable in the longer term, our workers need to be more productive," it said.
The report said the number of people who lost their jobs in 1996 rose sharply to 10,596 from 8,788 the previous year.
But 71 percent of the people who lost their jobs in the first three quarters of the year were re-employed by December.
"Singapore continued to enjoy (almost) full employment in 1996. The unemployment rate averaged 2.0 percent, same as in 1995," the report said.
It said the labour shortage eased, with the job vacancy rate falling to 4.8 percent in 1996 from the previous year's 5.2 percent.
Growth in the number of jobs slowed to 102,600 against an increase of 109,000 in 1995.

"With the exception of manufacturing, all major sectors generated net increases in jobs," the report said. "The economy is forecast to grow between 5.0 to 7.0 percent in 1997. Demand for labour is therefore expected to remain strong."
